venues.name: Playfair Library
venues.address: Old College, South Bridge, Edinburgh EH8 9YL

events.title: Preview: Dàna with Ellie Beaton
events.blurb: Start your Festival with the sounds of these award-winning, emerging Scottish folk artists.

events.title: [seagull]
events.blurb: Anton Chekhov’s The Seagull takes on new meaning in a Flemish Sign Language reimagining.

events.title: A Trial – after An Enemy of the People
events.blurb: Award-winning Brazilian director Christiane Jatahy returns to the Festival with a radical sequel to Henrik Ibsen’s An Enemy of the People, featuring Golden Globe-nominated actor Wagner Moura.

events.title: The Legacy of Slavery
events.blurb: Experience the first international exhibition from one of America’s premier cultural institutions, the Legacy Museum.

events.title: Dunedin Consort
events.blurb: The acclaimed Baroque ensemble performs Festival co-commission, Passion of Mary Magdalene by Tansy Davies.

events.title: Hostile
events.blurb: Everyday objects come to life in this family-friendly one-man Spaghetti Western.

events.title: Opening Concert: All Rise
events.blurb: Start your Festival with this resplendent jazz symphony embodying the human condition from Jazz at Lincoln Center and its Musical Director, Wynton Marsalis.

events.title: The Galloping Cure
events.blurb: Opera Ventures Productions and Scottish Opera present a bold new opera for the opioid age.

events.title: Jason Max Ferdinand Singers
events.blurb: Start your day with a stunning programme of spirituals, folk songs and hymns.

events.title: Gershwin & Bartók
events.blurb: Join 'some of the best young orchestral players in America' (The New York Times), in the second year of our collaboration with Carnegie Hall.

events.title: First Night at The Hub
events.blurb: Join violinist Nicola Benedetti and musicians from across the Festival for a surprise late-night lineup.

events.title: Beth Taylor & Hamish Brown
events.blurb: Hear evocative musical depictions of iconic female figures from myth, in the Festival debut of Scottish mezzo soprano Beth Taylor.

events.title: The Global Ideas Stage
events.blurb: Join us for an unconventional, dramatic, inquisitive and convivial conversation, inspired by our Festival theme.

events.title: JLCO plays Duke Ellington
events.blurb: A rare opportunity to experience Duke Ellington’s monumental jazz symphony, Black, Brown and Beige.

events.title: Up Late: Jazz Jam
events.blurb: Experience an energetic late-night jam, led by pianist Joe Webb and drummer Domo Branch, featuring our Rising Stars of Jazz.

events.title: JLCO with Yuja Wang
events.blurb: A world exclusive collaboration between classical superstar pianist Yuja Wang and the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra.

events.title: Sean Shibe
events.blurb: The Scottish guitarist’s Festival debut explores Spanish and British music across five centuries.

events.title: Brass Fanfare: A Tribute to John Wallace
events.blurb: Join brass players from across Scotland in tribute to star trumpeter, composer and educator John Wallace.

events.title: Mark & Maggie O'Connor
events.blurb: Enjoy an evening of dazzling fiddle tunes from two Grammy winners, celebrating the depth and beauty of American genres.

events.title: This Shining Night
events.blurb: The Edinburgh Festival Chorus joins with our Rising Stars for a programme of American music from the 20th and 21st centuries.

events.title: Venice Baroque Orchestra & Andrea Marcon
events.blurb: Celebrate the beauty of Baroque orchestral music with the Venice Baroque Orchestra and its founder-director Andrea Marcon.

events.title: Sounds of Ihsane
events.blurb: Immerse yourself in the musical worlds of North Africa and the Middle East.

events.title: Beethoven 7 & Ortiz
events.blurb: Join the LA Phil, conductor Gustavo Dudamel and singers from the Los Angeles Master Chorale for a feast of sonic beauty.

events.title: INALA
events.blurb: INALA celebrates South Africa’s rich cultural heritage through powerful Zulu harmonies, exhilarating choreography and moving storytelling.

events.title: Four Walls and a Roof
events.blurb: Lebanese artist duo Lina Majdalanie and Rabih Mroué weave together the story of McCarthy era censorship and modern-day repression of free speech.

events.title: Up Late with Gnoss
events.blurb: Experience the livewire instrumental skills and evocative songwriting of one of Scotland’s fastest-rising contemporary folk bands.

events.title: Art of Listening Workshops
events.blurb: Join us for our renowned Art of Listening workshops, crafted to bring adults and children closer to classical music through a shared experience.

events.title: Death of Gesualdo
events.blurb: Outstanding vocal ensemble The Gesualdo Six explores the chilling music and life story of composer Carlo Gesualdo in a multi-media theatrical piece.

events.title: Angels in America
events.blurb: Internationaal Theater Amsterdam reimagines Tony Kushner’s masterpiece in an epic performance.

events.title: Beethoven 6 & Adès
events.blurb: The LA Phil and conductor Gustavo Dudamel contrast Beethoven’s ‘Pastoral’ symphony with Thomas Adès’s The Divine Comedy.

events.title: Family Concert
events.blurb: Discover the magic of classical music in this joyful concert for children and their grown-ups.

events.title: Mozart’s Don Giovanni
events.blurb: Experience Mozart’s great opera of seduction, trickery and retribution.

events.title: Up Late with Mark O'Connor & Gustavo Dudamel
events.blurb: Discover a surprise lineup of musicians from across the Festival, led by string virtuoso Mark O’Connor and superstar conductor Gustavo Dudamel.

events.title: Steven Osborne
events.blurb: Steven Osborne performs works by Alfred Brendel’s beloved Schubert, alongside contemporary gems from Scottish composers James MacMillan and Judith Weir.

events.title: Classical Jam with Nicola Benedetti
events.blurb: You get to decide the music in this innovative, spontaneous concert.

events.title: Rising Stars of Voice with Louise Alder
events.blurb: Rising and established talents join forces for an exceptional recital of vocal music, including Johannes Brahms’s dramatic Neue Liebeslieder.

events.title: Ihsane
events.blurb: Award-winning choreographer Sidi Larbi Cherkaoui explores grief and connection while paying homage to North Africa and the Middle East.

events.title: corto.alto
events.blurb: The Mercury Prize-nominated Scottish jazz artist performs an energetic gig, joined by a collective of outstanding musicians.

events.title: Kleio Quartet, Makoto Ozone & Sheku Kanneh-Mason
events.blurb: Cellist Sheku Kanneh-Mason and pianist Makoto Ozone join the Kleio Quartet for Schubert and Bartók.

events.title: Coleridge-Taylor's The Song of Hiawatha
events.blurb: Samuel Coleridge-Taylor’s choral masterpiece is performed for the first time at the Festival, with the Orchestre symphonique de Montréal and conductor Rafael Payare.

events.title: Paul Lewis
events.blurb: Pianist Paul Lewis pays tribute to his teacher and mentor, Alfred Brendel, in a recital of classical and early Romantic works.

events.title: Voices of Canada
events.blurb: Discover new vocal works paying tribute to Canada’s Indigenous peoples, alongside works from composers Gabriela Ortiz and Richard Strauss.

events.title: Derya Türkan & Friends
events.blurb: Experience the music of 17th-century Turkey, performed on traditional instruments by Aga Khan Master Musicians.

events.title: Haribo Kimchi
events.blurb: Take a seat at theatre-maker Jaha Koo’s snack bar to discover the delights of Korean cuisine and the difficulties of cultural assimilation.

events.title: HANG TIME
events.blurb: Pulitzer Prize finalist Zora Howard’s subversive and moving play takes a sharp look at racialised violence in America.

events.title: Maxim Emelyanychev & SCO Wind Soloists
events.blurb: Enjoy a programme of 20th-century French chamber music, performed by wind soloists from the Scottish Chamber Orchestra, with their conductor Maxim Emelyanychev on piano.

events.title: Beyond Tradition
events.blurb: Join an electrifying, all-female group that crosses musical borders: Yasamin Shahhosseini  on oud, Farah Kaddour on buzuq and Senny Camara on kora.

events.title: Senny Camara Ensemble
events.blurb: Revel in the enchanting sounds of West African traditional music from Senegalese kora player Senny Camara and her ensemble.

events.title: Vilde Frang & Friends
events.blurb: Violinist Vilde Frang leads a superb ensemble of classical and folk musicians in a programme of works inspired by Hungarian traditional music.

events.title: Come and Sing Bach Chorales - Friends & Family
Alisa Weilerstein plays the Cello Suites
events.blurb: Alisa Weilerstein performs the feat of playing all six of JS Bach’s dance-inspired Cello Suites.

events.title: Víkingur Ólafsson plays Bach & Beethoven
events.blurb: Grammy Award-winning pianist Víkingur Ólafsson performs Bach keyboard pieces and Beethoven sonatas.

events.title: Strauss’s Elektra
events.blurb: Greek tragedy meets modern psychology in Richard Strauss’s audacious opera.

events.title: EXXY
events.blurb: Dan Daw returns to the Festival with his bold and triumphant dance-theatre work.

events.title: Scottish Ensemble & Brìghde Chaimbeul
events.blurb: Smallpipes player Brìghde Chaimbeul and the genre-crossing Scottish Ensemble explore Celtic music and mythology.

events.title: Gringolts Quartet
events.blurb: Franz Schubert’s final quartet is interwoven with music by György Kurtág, celebrating his centenary.

events.title: Simon Thoumire: Scots Fiddle & Clarsach
events.blurb: Composer and concertinist Simon Thoumire takes Scottish folk tunes on a thrilling ride into the unknown, with breathtaking results.

events.title: The Golden Age of Hollywood
events.blurb: The Sinfonia of London and conductor John Wilson take you on a glorious journey through the Golden Age of Hollywood.

events.title: Jordi Savall: A Sea of Music
events.blurb: Journey through music from Europe, Africa and the Americas, from the Baroque period and beyond.

events.title: Pierre-Laurent Aimard
events.blurb: Pierre-Laurent Aimard honours the late Alfred Brendel, his regular musical partner, with a characteristically imaginative programme.

events.title: Verdi's A Masked Ball
events.blurb: Zurich Opera House presents Giuseppe Verdi’s tragicomic opera, A Masked Ball, filled with desire, treachery and political peril.

events.title: Al-Sirah Al-Hilaliyyah
events.blurb: Palestinian theatre company Khashabi Theatre reimagines an epic poem with physical theatre and live music.

events.title: Camilla George
events.blurb: Experience a hypnotising blend of Afrofuturism, hip hop and jazz with visionary saxophonist and composer Camilla George.

events.title: Taverna Miresia – Mario, Bella, Anastasia
events.blurb: Discover a surreal tragedy in this visually stunning performance from emerging star of European theatre, Mario Banushi.

events.title: Julie Roset & Susan Manoff
events.blurb: Experience an inspired selection of songs from the French Belle Époque and beyond, sung by one of today’s most vibrant sopranos.

events.title: Mahler’s Das klagende Lied
events.blurb: Seize a rare chance to hear Gustav Mahler’s epic cantata Das klagende Lied (The Song of Lamentation).

events.title: When Prophecy Fails
events.blurb: Hypnotic physical theatre and dazzling production design combine to tell the tale of a doomsday cult, and what happens when belief is shattered.

events.title: Routes to Roots
events.blurb: Scottish violinist Catriona Price and Argentinian musicians El Guapo present a genre-defying celebration of music making.

events.title: Clown Show
events.blurb: Roll up, roll up for theatre-maker Geoff Sobelle’s contemporary portrait of America as a falling-apart circus.

events.title: Pavel Haas Quartet
events.blurb: Europe meets the US in a celebration of the string quartet, with music from Dvořák, Korngold and Martinů.

events.title: Orchestra Baobab
events.blurb: Experience the entrancing rhythms of Senegal’s legendary dance band.

events.title: Colin Currie Group plays Steve Reich
events.blurb: The experts in Steve Reich’s minimalist music celebrate of more than half of century of his work.

events.title: Mere Mortals
events.blurb: San Francisco Ballet presents a provocative myth for the AI age, in their futuristic retelling of Pandora’s Box.

events.title: RÓIS
events.blurb: RÓIS brings her experimental sound to The Hub, blending folk music, ancient Irish rituals and addictive electronic beats.

events.title: Members of the Berliner Philharmoniker
events.blurb: Players from the Berliner Philharmoniker perform an elegant and intimate programme of 19th- and 20th-century chamber works.

events.title: Berliner Philharmoniker: Elgar & Tchaikovsky
events.blurb: The Berliner Philharmoniker and Chief Conductor Kirill Petrenko open their residency with Tchaikovsky’s Fourth Symphony and Elgar’s ‘Enigma Variations’

events.title: Dementia-Friendly Concert
events.blurb: Experience a relaxed atmosphere and lively music with our Scottish Rising Stars of Jazz.

events.title: Berliner Philharmoniker: Closing Concert
events.blurb: Experience ‘the world’s greatest orchestra’ (LA Times) performing with award-winning soloist Augustin Hadelich in the final concert of their residency.

events.title: Up Late with Donald Shaw
events.blurb: Let your hair down at the last night at The Hub, with Capercaillie-founding folk musician Donald Shaw and friends.
